first_impression.reaction: So it's Corfu now. The opening tells me the island splits into five areas and that the choice comes down to guest numbers, the kind of ceremony and the view. Calm, plain English, no gushing. I'll read it properly, top to bottom.

journey.quote: July and August are the driest and hottest months in Corfu, and wildfires occur from June to September, so plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback for a summer date.
journey.reaction: Good. Heat and fires mentioned up front, not hidden at the bottom. I'm already thinking of Mum sitting in the sun at three in the afternoon.

journey.section: Corfu wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Sea view setting | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Rooms on site | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Eight columns on an iPad. I had to pinch and slide it sideways, and a lot of boxes just say 'Not published'. I'll print it or look at it on the computer with my husband.

journey.section: How to compare Corfu venues like for like
journey.quote: Rooms matter more than usual when most guests fly long-haul from Australia.
journey.reaction: Exactly right. After twenty-odd hours of flying, nobody older wants to be ferried between a hotel and a venue every day.

journey.section: How to compare Corfu venues like for like
journey.quote: At Atlantica Grand Mediterraneo it means the resort hosts only one wedding on your chosen day, not that the resort closes to other guests.
journey.reaction: Thank you. That's the sort of fine print I'd have missed, and it's the sort of thing people pay for and then feel cheated about.

journey.quote: Its published terms are dated 2023, so ask for current terms.
journey.reaction: Honest. They're not pretending old paperwork is current. I trust a page more when it tells me what might be out of date.

journey.quote: A reception hall for 200 is the bad-weather backup for the poolside reception, with the decision made by 11:00 on the day.
journey.reaction: A real rain plan with a time on it. That's what I want from every venue, not just this one.

journey.quote: Curfews, minimum nights, music rules and the rain plan are not published for any Kommeno venue. Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
journey.reaction: Fine, someone is responsible for checking. But I notice access for elderly or less mobile guests isn't on that list, here or anywhere else.

journey.quote: Event capacity and house rules for both south-east venues are not published; your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
journey.reaction: This is the fifth time I've read nearly the same sentence after an area. By now my eyes slide past it.

journey.quote: A hilltop house in the olive groves, looking inland to the mountain on one side.
journey.reaction: Lovely, but 'hilltop' and 'early 1700s' both make me think steps and uneven paths. My mother uses a walking frame. Not one of the ten venues says whether she can get from her room to the ceremony.

journey.quote: Kalami is the village the Durrell family chose as their home while Gerald Durrell wrote his best-known books, and the resort looks straight onto it.
journey.reaction: Oh, I loved The Durrells on the ABC. That's the first time I've actually pictured myself there.

journey.quote: Adults only shapes who can stay on site, so check it against your guest list before you fall for the view.
journey.reaction: Straight to the point. My sister's grandchildren are coming, so that settles that one before anyone gets attached.

journey.quote: For a wedding, the couple must be at the resort at least three working days before the date, not counting arrival day, public holidays and weekends, and two working days after.
journey.reaction: That's a week of accommodation before anyone's said a word about a dress. Useful to know now, because it changes what this costs us and how much leave my daughter needs.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: Second, build a rest day in before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Sensible. But the airport section only mentions car, bus and taxi. I'd want to know someone is arranging proper transfers for the older guests, not leaving them to queue for a taxi.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the overall advice level is "Exercise normal safety precautions", and it warns guests to take care swimming because of boat traffic, strong currents and marine life, and to swim at patrolled beaches where possible.
journey.reaction: Good to see the government's travel advice quoted and dated. I'll pass the swimming bit on to my brother-in-law, who thinks he's still twenty.

journey.quote: For a summer date, that means a shaded ceremony spot, a later start, water for guests and an indoor or covered fallback agreed with the venue in advance.
journey.reaction: Practical, and it doesn't frighten me off. What it doesn't mention is travel or medical insurance, which is the first thing I'd sort for Mum in that heat.

journey.quote: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only ones issued in their own country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, where to get it and whether it needs an authentication or apostille.
journey.reaction: I read that twice. One long sentence with three questions in it, and I still don't know who actually does the paperwork: us, the venue or the Advisor.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, fee in writing. That's the paragraph I'd show my husband. I'd still want to speak to that person on the phone before anything is paid.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have level paths, lifts or few steps between rooms, ceremony and reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
Who arranges airport transfers for older guests, rather than leaving them to the bus or a taxi queue?
What travel or medical insurance should older guests have for a summer wedding in Corfu?
Who actually prepares and lodges the legal paperwork, such as the CNI: the venue, the Wedded Advisor or us?
Who reads the venue contract if it is in Greek and priced in euros, and how is the venue deposit held?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Corfu time?
Is the first step a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked or paid?
would_share_with: My husband, with the closing section (fee in writing, AUD) and Atlantica's stay rule marked, since he'll ask what the extra nights cost
My daughter, with the adults-only note on San Antonio and the 'exclusive use' paragraph
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat and wildfire section and the Smartraveller swimming warning

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: A named person, AUD and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it said plainly that a real person rings me first, before anything is booked, and that they will check which venues suit my mother's mobility.

top_3_changes: Add access for less mobile guests (level paths, lifts, steps between rooms, ceremony and reception) to the venue 'Not published' lines or to the list of things the Wedded Advisor confirms in writing; flag the hilltop estate in particular.
In 'Getting to Corfu' and 'When to marry', add a line on organised transfers for older guests and on travel and medical insurance for a summer date.

Split the CNI sentence in the legal section into a short list and say who handles the paperwork in practice; trim or vary the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date' line after each area so it lands once, firmly.

checks.check: Every journey point and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing lines and unprinted prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

Journey types limited to the allowed enum; turn_offs_found empty because no persona turn-off was genuinely triggered (responsibility is covered by the Wedded Advisor lines; deposits and contracts are deferred business details)

open_questions.question: Accessibility for elderly guests is again this persona's main content gap: no Corfu venue mentions it, and The Courti Estate is a hilltop 1700s house. Unlike the Crete draft, this one also never mentions travel insurance or organised transfers. Treat accessibility and insurance as should-fix? Deposit, contract language and on-the-day contact are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
